detours.why: D-666 ARM B: this B.Cu segment TERMINATES at the barrel (59.300,106.300) the same spec removes.  Relaying it between its own two ends asks the router to reach a site that is reserved and a bond that is gone; ARM A asked exactly that and got NO_PATH at 0.300 mm inside a 5.180 mm budget.  It is a stub of a removed bond, so it is REMOVED AND NOT PUT BACK and the gate's inert_removal_priced clause prices it.

note: D-667 ARM H -- ARM G's spec with the REQUEST ORDER REVERSED.  Arm G asked /IR_TX_GPIO16 /SX1262_CS_N /WAKE_INT_N, in that order, because D-661 records 'the evicted net is requested FIRST'.  Both evicted nets routed -- /IR_TX_GPIO16, and /SX1262_CS_N at 116.669 mm / 9 vias against its accepted 68.405 mm / 5 -- and /WAKE_INT_N came back NO_PATH between two islands whose escapes both exist (24 src, 11 dst): they took the pocket back everywhere the reservation does not reach, and a lane drawn along a route does not reach that route's own PAD ESCAPES.  D-661's rule is written for the case where the EVICTED net is the one at risk.  Here the requested net is, so it is asked FIRST -- /WAKE_INT_N /IR_TX_GPIO16 /SX1262_CS_N -- and the other two rebuild around copper that is already on the board, which is a stronger obstacle than any reservation.  Same three GND units, same per-layer lane.
